# Booster

> Booster plans and runs PHP and Laravel upgrades one hop at a time on Rector, gates every hop with your tests on the target PHP, and never commits or pushes for you.

**Boosts your versions.** One dose at a time, and every dose gets a stamp.

**Not to be confused with:** Booster moves an app to a newer PHP or framework version; Pinstripe's Rector set only modernises code within the PHP version the app already runs.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

Development happens on Wayne State's GitLab; this repository is a release mirror. Changes land there first.

> A booster shot keeps your immunity current. This one keeps your PHP current, and it stings less.

Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/booster/blob/HEAD/site/index.html), a static page you can open in a browser or serve from `site/`.
On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/booster/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.

Booster is WELD's upgrade tool. It plans the hops that take a WSU PHP app from the PHP or Laravel version it runs now
to one the version policy still supports, and it runs them one at a time: [Rector](https://getrector.com) rewrites the
code, Booster raises the constraints in `composer.json`, and the app's own tests must pass on the target PHP before the
next hop starts. It stands on `rector/rector` and `driftingly/rector-laravel` and adds only the ordering, the cap, the
gate, the advisory scans and a few WSU recipes.

Booster edits your working copy and prints a report. It never commits to, pushes or opens a merge request on your app (the only merge requests it opens are its own hop-data refresh on Booster itself): a person reads
the diff and merges it.

Every page below is Markdown. The HTML pages send the same Markdown to a client that asks for `text/markdown`. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit from the README and the pages; do not edit.

## Pages

- [Booster: Boosts your versions.](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/index.md): Booster plans and runs PHP and Laravel upgrades one hop at a time on Rector, gates every hop with your tests on the target PHP, and never commits or pushes for you.

## Prompts

- [Get started with Booster](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-get-started): Clones Booster next to your app, runs detect and plan, and reports back. Nothing in your app changes. The prompt itself is in https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [Upgrade a raw PHP app](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-raw-php): Plans the PHP hops, scans for what will break and does a dry run. The real run waits until you say so. The prompt itself is in https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [Upgrade a raw PHP app with a Vue front end](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-raw-php-vue): Plans the PHP hops and the Node pin, and stages the Vue 2 to 3 move: the compat build, then the codemod, with a person doing the Vue work. The prompt itself is in https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [Upgrade a Laravel app with Blade](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-blade): Laravel and PHP hops in the order that keeps a supported pair at every step, and SESAME if the app still signs in with wayne-cas. The prompt itself is in https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [Upgrade a Laravel app with Vue islands](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-blade-vue): The Laravel and PHP hops, the Node pin, and Mix to Vite when the plan lands on Laravel 9 or newer. The prompt itself is in https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [Upgrade a Laravel app with Inertia](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-inertia-vue): The Laravel and PHP hops and the Node pin, with the Inertia checks a person still does by hand. The prompt itself is in https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
